column4: Salutations to Lord Ganesha!
Of this hymn named Sri Rama Raksha Stotra,
The sage is Budha Kaushika,
The deity is Lord Sri Sita Ramachandra,
The poetic meter is Anushtup,
The power (shakti) is Sita,
The pivot is Sri Hanuman,
To please Sri Ramachandra, the recitation of Rama Raksha Stotra is employed.
Meditation
Meditate upon the One whose arms extend up to the knees, who holds a bow and arrow; who is seated in the lotus posture,
Adorning yellow garments; having eyes which are more pleasing than the petals of a freshly-bloomed lotus; who is pleasant,
One whose sight is fixed on the lotus face of Sita seated on His left thigh; who resembles a cloud (in complexion),
Bejewelled with various magnificent ornaments; who possesses large matted tresses, Lord Ramachandra!
The deeds of Lord Raghunatha are vast, extending over a hundred crore,
Even a single syllable (describing His glory) is capable of destroying the greatest of sins!
Meditate upon Lord Rama, who is dark as the blue lotus; lotus-eyed,
Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana; adorned with a crown of matted hair!
One who bears the sword, quiver, bow and arrow; who destroys the ones that move about during the night (demons),
(Meditate upon) the unborn Supreme One, who appeared by His own divine play to protect the world!
Rama Raksha Stotra shall be recited by the learned; It annihilates sins and grants all desires,

column2: शिरो मे राघवः पातु भालं दशरथात्मजः ॥४॥
column3: śirō mē rāghavaḥ pātu bhālaṃ daśarathātmajaḥ ॥4॥
column4: May Raghava (Raghu's descendant) protect my head; May Dasharatha’s son protect the forehead!
May Kausalya's son protect the eyes; May Vishwamitra’s dearest protect the ears,
May the saviour of the ‘Yajna’ protect the nose; May the One affectionate to Sumitra’s son (Lakshmana) protect the mouth!
May the Treasure of knowledge protect the tongue; May the One venerated by Bharata protect the throat,
May the One with divine weapons protect the shoulders; May the One who broke Lord Shiva’s bow protect the arms!
May the consort of Sita Devi protect the hands; May the conqueror of Jamadagni’s son (Parasurama) protect the heart,
May the slayer of demon Khara protect the torso; May Jambavan’s refuge protect the navel!
May Sugriva’s Lord protect the hips; May Hanuman’s Master protect the femurs,
May the noblest of the Raghu scion protect the thighs; the destroyer of the demons' clan!
May the One who built the bridge protect the knees; May the destroyer of the ten-faced one (Ravana) protect the shanks,
May the One who bestowed prosperity to Vibhishana protect the feet; May Lord Rama protect the entire body!

column2: एतां रामबलोपेतां रक्षां यः सुकृती पठेत् ।
column3: ētāṃ rāmabalōpētāṃ rakṣāṃ yaḥ sukṛtī paṭhēt ।
column4: This hymn of protection is endowed with the strength of Lord Rama; whoever, being virtuous, recites it,

column2: स चिरायुः सुखी पुत्री विजयी विनयी भवेत् ॥१०॥
column3: sa cirāyuḥ sukhī putrī vijayī vinayī bhavēt ॥10॥
column4: He shall be long-lived, happy, blessed with progeny, victorious, and modest!
In the netherworld, on the earth, and in the sky, those who wander and move stealthily,
They are unable to even behold the one who is shielded by the names of Lord Rama!
‘Rama,’ ‘Ramabhadra,’ or ‘Ramachandra’ - by meditating thus,

column2: नरो न लिप्यते पापैः भुक्तिं मुक्तिं च विन्दति ॥१२॥
column3: narō na lipyatē pāpaiḥ bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca vindati ॥12॥
column4: A person is not stained by sins; attains both worldly enjoyment and liberation!
(This hymn) is safeguarded by the world-conquering, single mantra - the name of 'Rama',
Whoever bears (this hymn) in his throat; in his hands shall lie all accomplishments!
This hymn known as ‘Vajrapanjara’ (diamond cage) and ‘Rama Kavacha’ (armour of Rama); whoever recollects it,
His command is never obstructed; he attains victory and auspiciousness everywhere!
As instructed, in a dream by Lord Shiva, this Rama Raksha Stotra,
Likewise, it was inscribed at dawn, upon waking, by Sage Budha Kaushika!
The grove of wish-fulfilling trees; the cessation of all misfortunes,

column2: अभिरामस्त्रिलोकानां रामः श्रीमान् स नः प्रभुः ॥१६॥
column3: abhirāmastrilōkānāṃ rāmaḥ śrīmān sa naḥ prabhuḥ ॥16॥
column4: The most pleasing of the three worlds, Lord Rama, the glorious One - He is our Lord!
The two youths (Rama and Lakshmana); radiantly beautiful; tender yet incredibly powerful,
With eyes expansive as lotus flowers; clad in garments of bark and dark deerskin!
(Those two) who subsisted on fruits and roots; mastered their senses; practised austerity; adhered to celibacy,
These two sons of Dasharatha - the brothers, Rama and Lakshmana!
They are the refuge for all living beings; the greatest among all bowmen,
May the vanquishers of the demon clan, the exalted Ones of the Raghu dynasty protect us!
With their bows drawn and ready to strike; wielding powerful arrows; bearing quivers that have inexhaustible arrows,

column2: रक्षणाय मम रामलक्ष्मणावग्रतः पथि सदैव गच्छताम् ॥२०॥
column3: rakṣaṇāya mama rāmalakṣmaṇāvagrataḥ pathi sadaiva gacchatām ॥20॥
column4: For my protection, may Lord Rama and Lakshmana always lead the way before me on my path!
Ready and armed with an armour, sword, bow and arrow; the youthful One,
Who moves ahead; may Lord Rama, along with Lakshmana, protect us and our cherished desires!
Rama, the son of Dasharatha; the valiant; the companion of Lakshmana, the mighty One,
Who is a descendant of Kakutstha; the Complete Being; the son of Kausalya, the best among the clan of Raghu!
One who is known through Vedanta (the ultimate knowledge); the Lord of sacrifices; the Supreme Being glorified in the puranas,
The consort of Janaki; the glorious; One with unfathomable prowess!
Thus, one who chants these (names) daily, as My devotee endued with faith,
Attains more merit than that of an ‘Ashvamedha Yajna’, without a doubt!
Lord Rama, who is dark-hued like the blades of Durva grass; lotus-eyed; clothed in yellow garments,

column2: स्तुवन्ति नामभिर्दिव्यैः न ते संसारिणो नराः ॥२५॥
column3: stuvanti nāmabhirdivyaiḥ na tē saṃsāriṇō narāḥ ॥25॥
column4: People who sing His glorious names are not bound by the cycles of birth and death!
Lord Rama, the elder brother of Lakshmana, the Supreme among the Raghu clan, the charming consort of Sita,
The descendant of Kakutstha; the ocean of compassion; the repository of virtues; the beloved of ascetics; the righteous One,
The Supreme King; One who is firmly committed to truth; Dasharatha’s son; dark-hued; the embodiment of tranquility,
I bow to the One who delights the world; the ornament of the Raghu lineage; Raghava; the enemy of Ravana!
(Salutations) to Lord Rama, Ramabhadra, Ramachandra, the One who is the source of all wisdom,
Salutations to the Lord of the Raghu dynasty, the ruler; the husband of Sita!
O Sri Rama, Rama, the joy of the Raghu dynasty, Rama, Rama,
O Sri Rama, Rama, the elder brother of Bharata, Rama, Rama,
O Sri Rama, Rama, who is fierce in battle, Rama, Rama,

column2: श्रीराम राम शरणं भव राम राम ॥२८॥
column3: śrīrāma rāma śaraṇaṃ bhava rāma rāma ॥28॥
column4: O Sri Rama, Rama, be my refuge, Rama, Rama!
Upon the feet of Sri Ramachandra, with my mind, I meditate,
About the feet of Sri Ramachandra, with my words, I sing,
To the feet of Sri Ramachandra, with my head, I bow,
In the feet of Sri Ramachandra, I take refuge!
My mother is Lord Rama, my father is Sri Ramachandra,
My Lord is Rama, my companion is Sri Ramachandra,
To me, everything is Sri Ramachandra, the compassionate One!

column2: नान्यं जाने नैव जाने न जाने ॥३०॥
column3: nānyaṃ jānē naiva jānē na jānē ॥30॥
column4: I do not know, indeed, anyone other than Him!

column2: दक्षिणे लक्ष्मणो यस्य वामे च जनकात्मजा ।
column3: dakṣiṇē lakṣmaṇō yasya vāmē ca janakātmajā ।
column4: On whose right is Lakshmana; On whose left is the daughter of King Janaka (Sita),
On whose front stands the son of Maruta (Hanuman); I bow to the delight of Raghu clan (Rama)!
One who is delightful to the world; courageous in the battlefield,
With lotus-like eyes; the Lord of the Raghu dynasty,
Embodiment of compassion; the bestower of grace,
I seek refuge in Lord Sri Ramachandra!
One who is as swift as the mind (Lord Hanuman); equivalent to the speed of ‘Maruta’ (the wind),
Conqueror of the senses, the Supreme among the wise,
Born of ‘Vayu’ (wind); the chief of the monkey army,
I seek refuge in the messenger of Lord Rama!
Chirping 'Rama Rama,' the sweet and melodious syllables,
Perched upon the branch of poetry, to that cuckoo bird named Valmiki, I bow!
The remover of all dangers; the bestower of all wealth and prosperity,
One who delights the world, Sri Rama, to Him, I repeatedly prostrate!
That which destroys the seeds of worldly existence; bestows the wealth of happiness and prosperity,
The terrifying sound that frightens the messengers of Lord Yama is the thunderous chant of ‘Rama Rama’!

column2: रामो राजमणिः सदा विजयते रामं रमेशं भजे
column3: rāmō rājamaṇiḥ sadā vijayatē rāmaṃ ramēśaṃ bhajē
column4: Rama, the jewel amongst kings, eternally triumphs; I worship Rama, the Lord of Lakshmi,
By Rama, the army of the night-rovers (demons) were defeated; Salutations to Lord Rama!
There is no greater refuge than Lord Rama; I am a servant of Lord Rama,

column2: रामे चित्तलयः सदा भवतु मे भो राम मामुद्धर ॥३७॥
column3: rāmē cittalayaḥ sadā bhavatu mē bhō rāma māmuddhara ॥37॥
column4: In Lord Rama, may my mind incessantly repose; O Rama, please uplift me!

column2: राम रामेति रामेति रमे रामे मनोरमे ।
column3: rāma rāmēti rāmēti ramē rāmē manōramē ।
column4: By chanting 'Rama, Rama, Rama', I rejoice in Lord Rama, who delights my heart,
That name (Rama) is equivalent to the thousand names (Vishnu Sahasranama), O beautiful-faced One!
Thus concludes Rama Raksha Stotram composed by Sage Budha Kaushika!
May this be an offering to Devi Sita and Lord Ramachandra!
